summary: Anil Kumar works in computational linguistics and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Hyderabad in 2012, where he also held a post.

Anil Vidyalankar (b. 1928) is an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher. Educated at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Columbia University, and the University of Delhi (PhD), he founded Sandhaan in 1988 and served as its director (attested 1999).

Animesh Prakash specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA from the University of Hong Kong (2016–2017) and held assistant professorships at Somaiya Vidyavihar University (2014–2018) and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (2018).

Animesh Roy is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed an integrated MA in Sanskrit at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Educational and Research Institute (2017–2022) and became a research scholar at Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit in 2022.
Animisha Tewari specializes in philosophy and Indology. She completed a BA at Miranda House (2017–2020) and earned an MA from the University of Delhi (2020–2022).

Anirban Dash specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. At the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, he served as a research assistant (attested 2003–2005) and later as Associate Professor of Sanskrit (attested 2026).
Anita is an Indology scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Lucknow. In 2009, she held a post as professor at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

Anjay Dhanawade works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Mumbai (BA, 1996–1999), Savitribai Phule Pune University (MA, 2000–2002), and Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (PhD, 2010–2016), serving as assistant professor at Lokavikas Samajik Sanstha (2010–2023).
Ankita Chakraborty is an Indology scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Bijoya Goswami (attested 2026). She served as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
Ankita Nanda specializes in Indology. She earned her PhD from Panjab University in 2022, where she was also a senior research scholar that same year.

Ankur Barua specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Dorothy C. Wong and earned degrees from Manipal Academy of Higher Education (MD 2003), Sikkim Manipal University (MBAIT 2007), and the University of Hong Kong (MBuddStud 2009), holding a post at the University of Delhi (attested 2012).

Ann Appleby Hazlewood specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned a Master of Arts at the Australian National University (attested 1983), where she studied under supervisors Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus.
Ann Gleig works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University (attested 2010) under the supervision of Jeffrey J. Kripal.

Ann Grodzins Gold (b. 1946) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Chicago (BA, MA, PhD in anthropology), she held posts at Cornell University (~1988–1993) and Syracuse University (~1993).

Ann Heirman (b. 1965) works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held positions at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1995–2009) and Ghent University, where she became a professor, Centre for Buddhist Studies head (~2000), and director (2003–2012).

Ann Laura Stoler (b. 1949) studied at Barnard College (BA 1968–1972) and Columbia University (MA 1972–1976). She taught at University of Wisconsin-Madison (1983–1989) and University of Michigan (1989–2004), and was founding director at The New School (2004).

Anna Andreeva specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She has held posts at Heidelberg University and Ghent University, where she is attested as a permanent member in 2026.

Anna Aurelia Esposito studied Indology and Cultural Anthropology at Würzburg and Heidelberg, earning an MA at Tübingen (1998). She held posts at the University of Würzburg (attested 2012–2015) and the University of Zurich (attested 2026).

Anna Balikci-Denjongpa earned a PhD from SOAS University of London (2002) under Lionel Caplan, also studying with Lopen Dugyal and Gorlok Tulku. In 2002, she held posts at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and the Bulletin of Tibetology.

Anna Brown is a scholar of religious studies and a Zen student of Robert Kennedy (attested 2017). Attested in 2017, she served as political science department chair and social justice program director at Saint Peter's University.
